title: 理由与细节的展开
goal: 用原因、例子、对比和结果展开回答，并排除重复或偏离问题的细节。
exam: TOEFL iBT（2026 年 1 月起的新版）· 口语

points.label: 用理由和细节展开一个回答
判断内容是否对应问题

body.p: 展开是补充支持答案的新信息。The workshop was useful. It was very helpful. 只是重复评价。It showed me how to replace a loose handle. 说明了学到的具体技能。
细节要和问题相关。问活动为什么有效时，The room had white walls. 很具体，但没有说明效果。The checklist prevented us from missing a step. 说明了效果。

cards.title: 展开的来源
rows: 原因
说明答案为什么成立，不重复原来的评价。
I used a checklist because the procedure had several similar steps.
例子
用一次具体经历支持理由。
Last time, the list reminded me to tighten the final screw.
对比
比较两者的同一个方面，不只列出两个对象。
Without the list I skipped a step; with it I checked every joint.
结果
说明前面的做法带来了什么影响。
The loose joint was fixed, so the frame no longer wobbled.

cards.title: 空泛与具体
rows: The demonstration was useful.
The instructor showed how to align the hinge before tightening it.
动作及操作顺序
The schedule was better.
The new schedule left a free hour between the two rehearsals.
具体时间安排
The notes helped me.
The notes listed which cable belonged to each socket.
信息内容及用途
The group worked well.
One member measured while another recorded the dimensions.
成员分工
The practice was different.
Previously I copied the model; this time I explained each step aloud.
同一任务的前后对比
The change had a good result.
After we added labels, visitors found the right counter without asking.
可观察的结果

cards.title: 相关性与重复
rows: 直接支持
细节回答原因、方式或影响。
Why label drawers? → Labels show where each tool belongs.
只有同义重复
换了词，但没有增加事实或关系。
It is helpful. It is beneficial.
只有话题关联
属于同一话题，但不支持所问的观点。
Why label drawers? → The drawers are wooden.
例子范围过大
个人经历不能证明所有人都如此。
I found the labels useful. ≠ Everyone needs these labels.
关系缺失
两个事实之间要写出联系。
The labels were enlarged, so the names were readable from the doorway.
多余背景
背景要服务于问题，不为延长回答而添加。
Why enlarge labels? → The building opened years ago.

body.box:
Question: Why was the tool-sharing scheme useful?
Notes: members borrowed rarely used tools; each member avoided buying a separate set; the cupboard was painted green; the scheme began in winter.

Which detail best develops the answer 'It reduced expenses'?
1. Members did not need to purchase their own complete sets.
2. Members kept the tools in a green cupboard.
3. The scheme started during the winter term.
4. The cupboard contained tools used by members.

body.p: 第一项把 reduced expenses 展开为 avoided buying a separate set。柜子的颜色、开始的季节和存放地点都与项目有关，但没有说明开支为什么减少。

groups.text: Claim: Rotating the meeting chair broadened participation. Notes: different members led each week; previously one person always led; meetings used the same room.

options: The room stayed the same, but its use was weekly.
Leadership passed from one chair to several members.
Each chair used a different room for the same meeting.
The same person led before and after the change.
items.why: previously one person always led 和 different members led each week 是前后对比。第二项说的就是主持人从一人变成多人。

groups.text: Claim: The museum map improved navigation. Notes: exits were marked clearly; visitors stopped asking where to leave; maps were folded at the desk.

options: Staff folded maps near the visitors.
The map included the museum's exits.
Visitors no longer needed directions to the exits.
Visitors asked for exit directions more frequently.
items.why: visitors stopped asking where to leave 是导航改善后的结果，第三项与之对应。第二项说的是地图上的标注，是措施，不是结果。

groups.text: Claim: A shared equipment log prevented confusion. Notes: borrowers wrote their names; the log identified who had each item; its cover was red.

options: The log showed which borrower had each item.
The red cover made the log easy to find.
Each borrower kept a separate personal log.
The equipment log prevented all borrowing.
items.why: 依据是 the log identified who had each item，这就是避免混淆的方式。第一项是这句的同义改写。

groups.text: Claim: A rehearsal plan helped the quartet. Notes: difficult passages were marked; the players focused on them; the plan was helpful and useful.

items.stem: Which detail adds information beyond a positive evaluation?
options: The plan was helpful and useful to the quartet.
The players marked the passages they found easy.
The quartet practiced every passage equally.
Marked passages guided the players' practice.
items.why: 依据是 difficult passages were marked 和 the players focused on them。第四项说明了计划怎样帮助排练，不是重复 helpful。

groups.text: Question: Why was the morning delivery preferable? Notes: staff could unpack before customers arrived; the van was white; afternoon traffic was heavier; the shop used paper receipts.

items.stem: Which detail is unrelated to the timing advantage?
options: Unpacking finished before customers arrived.
Afternoon traffic tended to be heavier.
The delivery van was painted white.
Staff received goods while the shop was quiet.
items.why: before customers arrived 和 afternoon traffic was heavier 都和送货时间有关。the van was white 只说明车的外观，所以选第三项。

groups.text: Question: How did the garden rota reduce missed watering? Response: It helped a lot. It was helpful. It really helped.

options: The way the rota assigned or checked watering duties
The speaker's generally positive view of the rota
The activity that the rota was supposed to support
The fact that the speaker considered the rota helpful
items.why: 问题问的是 how，回答三次说 helped，没有说明方式。缺的是第一项：轮值表怎样分配或检查浇水的任务。

groups.text: Question: Why was the translation glossary useful? Notes: it kept key terms consistent; the same term appeared throughout the report; the report had a blue cover.

items.stem: Which detail supports the stated benefit?
options: The report was printed with a blue cover.
The glossary listed every word in the report.
Translators chose new terms in each chapter.
Each concept kept one term across the report.
items.why: 依据是 it kept key terms consistent 和 the same term appeared throughout the report。第四项说的就是术语前后一致。

groups.text: Question: Did the practice interview help with answering follow-up questions? Notes: the interviewer asked for reasons; the speaker learned to explain choices; the room had a large window.

items.stem: Which information belongs in the answer's explanation?
options: The size of the window in the interview room
The practice in giving reasons for choices
The questions the speaker asked the interviewer
The interviewer's own reasons for the choices
items.why: 依据是 the interviewer asked for reasons 和 the speaker learned to explain choices。第二项就是应对追问的练习，窗户只是背景。

lines.text: I prefer preparing a packing list for field visits. On my first visit I left the sample labels behind. With a list, I now check the labels before leaving. The field station also has a new entrance.

options: The station's old entrance versus its new entrance
Forgetting labels before versus checking them with a list
Preparing labels at home versus preparing them at the station
Taking samples on the first visit versus never taking them again
items.why: 依据是 I left the sample labels behind 和 I now check the labels before leaving。第二项比较的是同一件物品在用清单前后的处理。

lines.text: The student-run cinema changed its ticket system. I like the new system because seats are assigned in advance. Friends can choose adjacent seats instead of searching after they arrive. The foyer still displays old film posters.

items.stem: Which detail does not support the reason given for liking the system?
options: Friends can choose seats beside each other.
Seats are allocated before the audience arrives.
The foyer continues to display old posters.
Friends avoid searching for seats after arrival.
items.why: 喜欢的理由是座位提前分配。The foyer still displays old film posters 与这个理由无关，所以选第三项。

lines.text: The shared recipe file was helpful. When I cooked for a guest who avoided dairy, I found a version using vegetable stock instead of cream. The file made that substitution easy to locate.

items.stem: How is the general claim developed?
options: By describing one occasion when the file solved a problem
By repeating that every recipe in the file was helpful
By comparing two guests who avoided different foods
By claiming that all guests prefer stock to cream
items.why: 依据是 When I cooked for a guest who avoided dairy 和 The file made that substitution easy to locate。第一项说的就是这一次具体的使用经历。

lines.text: A language buddy asked how drawing diagrams helped me explain routes. I said that diagrams helped, and that they were helpful for routes. I also said I found them useful.

items.stem: What addition would address the missing development?
options: Another statement that diagrams are helpful
A stronger claim that diagrams are always useful
A repetition of the phrase explaining routes
An example of a turn the diagram helped explain
items.why: helped、helpful、useful 都只是重复评价。问题问的是 how，第四项的具体例子才能回答它。

groups.text: Question: Why did the choir use a seating chart? Notes: new singers could find their section; arrivals became quicker; the chart was printed on thick paper.

options: Arriving singers reached their places faster.
The paper used for the chart was relatively thick.
New singers drew the chart after each rehearsal.
The chart delayed arrivals by separating sections.
items.why: 依据是 arrivals became quicker，第一项是这一结果的同义改写。thick paper 只是纸张的特征。

groups.text: Question: Why was a quiet hour useful in the shared studio? Notes: interruptions had delayed detailed work; quiet hours protected concentration; the studio was upstairs.

items.stem: Which explanation links the cause to the benefit?
options: Being upstairs kept the studio away from noise.
Fewer interruptions let focused work continue.
Detailed work was done only during quiet hours.
Quiet hours increased the number of interruptions.
items.why: interruptions had delayed detailed work 是原来的问题，quiet hours protected concentration 是改善后的作用。第二项把两者连了起来。

groups.text: Question: How did a checklist improve the equipment return process? Response: It improved the process. The process became better. Returning equipment was improved.

items.stem: Which diagnosis follows from the response?
options: It supplies several separate causes of improvement.
It contrasts returns made by different groups.
It restates the improvement but never says how.
It gives a detailed result but no initial opinion.
items.why: improved、became better、was improved 都在重复同一个评价，没有说明清单怎样改变了归还过程。第三项指出的就是这一点。

groups.text: Question: Why did the book swap introduce separate shelves for children's books? Notes: families could find suitable titles quickly; volunteers sorted by age; the shelves stood near a mural.

items.stem: Which detail is background rather than support for easier selection?
options: Books were sorted according to readers' ages.
Families located age-appropriate titles more quickly.
Children's books occupied a separate set of shelves.
The shelves were positioned near a painted mural.
items.why: the shelves stood near a mural 只说明书架的位置，与挑选合适的书无关，所以选第四项。
